skill.name: error-handling
skill.description: Guides assistants to add robust error handling for async code, API calls, React components, and user-facing failures.
skill.summary: Apply clear error handling patterns for async code, React boundaries, fallbacks, logging, and user messages.
skill.author: Doyajin174

security_audit.summary: The static command findings are false positives from Markdown fences and TypeScript or TSX template literals. The hardcoded URLs are documentation references, and NODE_ENV access is a non-secret sample check. One semantic issue remains because the community skill grants Bash without a demonstrated need.

remediation.suggestion: Remove Bash from allowed-tools unless the skill documents a necessary command workflow. Keep permissions limited to the tools the guidance requires.

remediation.issue: Telemetry examples may include sensitive context
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to redact tokens, personal data, request bodies, and stack traces before sending errors to tracking services.

content.value_statement: Weak error handling hides failures and exposes technical messages to users. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward safer recovery patterns.
actual_capabilities: Shows try-catch patterns with logging, tracking, user feedback, and fallback returns.
Demonstrates error type branching for network, not found, authentication, and unexpected errors.
Provides TypeScript custom error class examples for operational errors.
Demonstrates React Error Boundary components and scoped boundary placement.
Covers Promise catch handling, Promise.allSettled, and graceful degradation flows.
Includes checklists for React components, API calls, and general error handling.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not an automated code validator.
Examples assume TypeScript, React, and an existing error tracking service.
It does not choose monitoring vendors or configure production observability.
It does not replace privacy review for logged errors or telemetry context.

use_cases.title: Harden API Calls
use_cases.description: Review request code for missing catch paths, user-safe messages, and fallback behavior.

use_cases.title: Add React Boundaries
use_cases.description: Plan where to place Error Boundaries so one component failure does not break the full app.

use_cases.title: Standardize Error Responses
use_cases.description: Create consistent error classes, message maps, and logging rules for a team codebase.

prompt_templates.title: Review Basic Error Handling
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one async function.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this async function for missing error handling. Suggest try-catch, user feedback, logging, and a simple fallback.

prompt_templates.title: Improve API Failure Paths
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of API request behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this API call flow. Separate network, not found, authentication, validation, and unexpected errors with user-safe messages.

prompt_templates.title: Design React Error Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend Error Boundary placement for this React screen. Include fallback UI behavior and logging for component failures.

prompt_templates.title: Create Error Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an application error handling strategy. Cover custom error types, message mapping, graceful degradation, telemetry, and review checklist items.

output_examples.input: A data loader leaves the page blank when a request fails.
output: Add a catch path that stores an error state and logs the failure.
Show a user-safe message with a retry action.
Return cached or empty fallback data when possible.

output_examples.input: A React dashboard crashes when one chart throws an error.
output: Wrap the chart area in a scoped Error Boundary.
Display a chart-specific fallback instead of replacing the whole page.
Send the captured error and component context to the tracking service.

output_examples.input: An app shows raw technical errors to users.
output: Map internal error codes to clear user messages.
Keep stack traces in developer logs only.
Use a default message for unexpected failures.

best_practices: Handle expected error types separately before using a generic fallback path.
Log enough context for developers while showing users simple recovery guidance.
Use scoped fallbacks so one failed feature does not break the whole screen.
anti_patterns: Do not leave catch blocks empty or silently ignore rejected promises.
Do not show stack traces or raw exception messages to end users.
Do not fail an entire page when a smaller fallback can keep useful content available.

faq.question: Does this skill write production error handling code automatically?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and review guidance. The assistant can draft code when you provide project context.

faq.question: Which languages does it focus on?
faq.answer: The examples focus on TypeScript and TSX, with React and async JavaScript patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with React Error Boundaries?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes boundary structure, fallback UI, and placement guidance for whole apps and smaller sections.

faq.question: Does it cover user-facing error messages?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends mapping internal errors to clear messages and avoiding technical details in the UI.

faq.question: Does it configure error tracking tools?
faq.answer: No. It assumes an error tracking service exists and shows where logging or capture calls belong.

faq.question: What should teams review before adopting it?
faq.answer: Teams should review logging privacy, telemetry redaction, and whether the Bash tool permission is necessary.
